title: Empirical Evaluation of a Validator‑Assisted LLM NetOps Pipeline: A Preregistered Paired Study with gpt‑5‑mini on 400 Intent→Configuration Tasks
abstract: We preregistered (CAND‑2026‑002) and executed a paired experiment comparing direct application of an LLM‑generated network configuration (Baseline) to a deterministic syntax/policy validator with at most one bounded LLM repair (Guarded). Using gpt‑5‑mini via a hosted NetOps adapter (hosted_netops_gvr_v1) on 400 public/synthetic intents (shared_initial_candidate semantics), we completed 800 emulator episodes with no infrastructure failures. All paired episodes were operationally successful under both arms (n11=400, n10=0, n01=0, n00=0). The paired difference (Guarded − Baseline)=0.00 (95% bootstrap percentile CI 0.00–0.00; 10k resamples, seed=1729); McNemar exact two‑sided p=1.0. Crucially, the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics produced identical candidates for both arms and the deterministic validator accepted every candidate (validator_reject_count=0, deterministic_repair_calls_invoked=0), rendering the Guarded intervention empirically inert on this task bank. We release the complete archived artifacts and hashes (principal file: execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256 871b297808ae2bb6b26260c99299d5c493afd3b03232ca4d92c39ca5ffaab865) and interpret this run as a reproducible boundary case that clarifies experimental‑design dependencies for future validator efficacy studies.

sections.introduction: Motivation and question. Large language models (LLMs) can translate high‑level NetOps intent into device CLI but can produce erroneous changes that threaten reachability, policy conformance, and availability. The generate→validate→repair design is widely advocated, yet quantitative, preregistered evidence measuring how lightweight automated validators reduce operational failures under realistic execution semantics is limited. Research question (preregistered): What is the paired difference in operational failure proportion when applying (A) a shared LLM candidate directly (Baseline) vs (B) the same candidate after a deterministic syntax/policy validator with at most one deterministic repair call (Guarded)? Contributions. (1) A fully preregistered (CAND‑2026‑002), archived paired experiment (400 intents, 800 episodes) using gpt‑5‑mini and a hosted NetOps adapter, with exact artifact hashes; (2) an explicit demonstration that choice of generation semantics (shared_initial_candidate) can render a guarded validator empirically inert; (3) reproducible artifacts and prescriptive design implications for future validator efficacy evaluations.
sections.related_work: Closest lines. Work on LLMs for intent→configuration, generate→validate‑repair architectures, and verifier‑guided correction motivated our design and preregistration. Representative, verified sources include a comprehensive NetOps/AIOps survey and architecture discussion (W4415071524), prior intent‑translation and LLM‑based configuration work (doi:10.1002/nem.2313), verifier‑guided IaC repair studies (doi:10.2139/ssrn.6608518; W7124141852), and formal verification and continuous compliance literature for network configs (W4401857375). These establish the operational stakes and motivate measuring the marginal value of lightweight validators under well‑specified generation semantics.
sections.methodology: Preregistration and frozen design. The preregistration (study_id=CAND‑2026‑002) was frozen prior to model calls and specified: paired design; primary estimand = P(failure|Baseline) − P(failure|Guarded) across 400 paired intents; generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate" (one identical candidate produced and reused by both arms); maximum_model_calls=800; analysis = McNemar exact two‑sided test and 95% bootstrap percentile confidence interval (10k resamples, seed=1729). Implementation. Adapter family: hosted_netops_gvr_v1; model: gpt‑5‑mini; transformation pipelines: direct_configuration_generation_v1 and generate_validate_repair_v1 (preregistered). For each intent: one shared model call produced a single candidate; Baseline applied that candidate; Guarded ran a deterministic syntax/policy validator against the same candidate and, only if the validator rejected, allowed one deterministic LLM repair call (bounded). Emulation and scoring. Changes were applied to sandboxed emulator replicas; an automated scorer marked operational failure (reachability loss or policy violation). All raw outputs, provider call records, validator traces, and per‑task scoring JSONs are archived. Key archived artifacts and verified hashes (see execution_manifest): execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256 871b297808ae2bb6b26260c99299d5c493afd3b03232ca4d92c39ca5ffaab865; analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 fad28887d8b3847baaebe368d178ba14986eaeb633d789dae1396bce3bf14abf; execution/execution_log.jsonl (validator logs), execution/transformation_manifest.json (validator rule set). Reproducibility policy. All per‑task provider call caches, scoring JSONs, and execution logs were preserved and their SHA‑256 hashes recorded in the execution_manifest.
sections.results: Execution outcomes (archived). completed_episode_count=800; completed_pair_count=400; model_calls_used=400; validator_reject_count=0; deterministic_repair_calls_invoked=0. Paired contingency (analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv): n11=400, n10=0, n01=0, n00=0. Confirmatory statistics (preregistered analyses): Baseline success rate = 400/400 = 1.0; Guarded success rate = 400/400 = 1.0; paired difference (Guarded − Baseline) = 0.00; bootstrap percentile 95% CI = [0.00, 0.00] (10,000 resamples, seed=1729); McNemar exact two‑sided p = 1.0. Diagnostic observation. Because generation_semantics was shared_initial_candidate and the deterministic validator accepted every identical candidate (validator_reject_count=0), the Guarded pipeline was not exercised (no repairs or rejections happened) and therefore the experiment does not provide evidence about validator efficacy on inputs that would be rejected. Representative artifacts. Example trace for task‑000001 (prompt → shared candidate → validator pass → scorer): execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt (SHA‑256 f8de4d6e...), execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json (SHA‑256 ffb47774...), execution/scoring/task-000001-guarded.json (SHA‑256 9e70f3a4...). The full execution_manifest lists every per‑task file and its SHA‑256.
sections.discussion: Interpretation as a boundary case. The numerical results are correct and fully reproducible from archived artifacts, but they reflect a boundary outcome: the preregistered shared_initial_candidate semantics produced identical candidates and the deterministic validator accepted them all, so Guarded had no opportunity to alter any outcome. Thus the study demonstrates that (i) generation semantics and task sampling determine whether a validator can be empirically tested, and (ii) an observed equivalence in this setup should be interpreted as an artifact of the experimental design rather than evidence that validators are unnecessary or ineffective in general. Design lessons for future preregistered evaluations (artifact‑grounded): (A) use independent_condition_generation=true to allow each arm to receive independently generated candidates so a validator can be exercised; (B) include small, preregistered injected positive controls (intents constructed to produce invalid candidates) to verify validator liveness; (C) sample tasks with known historical difficulty or adversarial patterns; (D) preserve and publish validator rule sets and decision logs (we archived these: execution/execution_log.jsonl and execution/transformation_manifest.json) so readers can audit why rejects did or did not occur. Threats to validity. Internal: prompt sensitivity and single‑model choice (gpt‑5‑mini) limit internal generality; deterministic validator behavior depends on exact rule set archived in execution/transformation_manifest.json. Construct: our operational failure definition (reachability loss or policy violation) depends on the emulator and scorer; scorer JSONs are archived (execution/scoring/*.json) so readers can inspect scoring thresholds. External: single model, single adapter, synthetic/public task bank, and emulated execution restrict generalization to production. Relevance. Even as a null/ boundary result, the run provides a reproducible empirical lesson: preregistered generation semantics are not neutral—they can make an intervention empirically inert—and artifact release enables others to rerun alternative preregistered designs.
sections.conclusion: We preregistered and executed a fully archived paired evaluation of direct LLM candidate application vs a deterministic validator + bounded repair across 400 intent→configuration tasks using gpt‑5‑mini. The observed outcome—complete concordance (n11=400) and zero validator rejects—shows this run is a reproducible boundary case: with shared_initial_candidate semantics the Guarded condition cannot be exercised unless the shared candidate is rejected. Accordingly, the primary contribution is methodological: (a) we provide a precise, hashed artifact trail that documents how experimental design choices (generation semantics, sampling) determine whether a validator can be empirically tested; (b) we recommend concrete preregistered design changes (independent generation, injected positive controls, targeted task sampling) for future validator‑efficacy studies. All artifacts and hashes required to reproduce this run are released (see execution_manifest and the principal file hashes cited below).

disclosure_statement: Mandatory Disclosure (artifact‑grounded). Human involvement and autonomy boundary: after an autonomy lock the autonomous system performed literature review, candidate study selection, preregistration (CAND‑2026‑002), code generation, experiment execution, analysis, peer‑review response, and manuscript drafting and revision. The Research Director selected the topic family (Generative AI / LLMs for NetOps) and approved pre‑lock infrastructure development; no human manually edited or rewrote technical manuscript content after the autonomy lock. Models and adapter: model=gpt‑5‑mini (calls via hosted NetOps adapter family hosted_netops_gvr_v1). Exact master prompts, system instructions, and generation templates used for each shared_initial candidate are archived in execution/raw_results.jsonl and in the provider call cache files recorded in execution_manifest. Preregistration/freeze: the preregistration (study_id=CAND‑2026‑002) was frozen before any model calls and specified the research question, confirmatory hypotheses (H1–H4), primary estimand (paired difference), generation_semantics=shared_initial_candidate, analysis plan (McNemar exact; bootstrap CI 10k resamples, seed=1729), sample size (400 paired intents), maximum_model_calls=800, retry policy, and stopping rules; the full preregistration object is archived in execution_manifest.preregistration. Framework and validator: experiments used hosted_netops_gvr_v1 to call gpt‑5‑mini; the deterministic syntax/policy validator and the bounded repair template are archived (execution/transformation_manifest.json and execution/execution_log.jsonl). Execution manifest and hashes: execution/raw_results.jsonl SHA‑256 871b297808ae2bb6b26260c99299d5c493afd3b03232ca4d92c39ca5ffaab865; analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv SHA‑256 fad28887d8b3847baaebe368d178ba14986eaeb633d789dae1396bce3bf14abf; representative response: execution/responses/task-000001-shared-initial.txt SHA‑256 f8de4d6e1a625e42ba4907440b4377c78949ed56446e5c73030bc267e56abfaf; scorer JSON: execution/scoring/task-000001-baseline.json SHA‑256 ffb47774de570d1f8417a3191ccaae87aac22ddcda4d246f3224e8ef6284c177. Technical restarts and failures: started_at_utc and completed_at_utc are recorded in execution_manifest; completed_episode_count=800; failed_episode_count=0; model_calls_used=400. Pre‑lock development: pre‑lock infrastructure development and rehearsal occurred but were explicitly excluded from final empirical evidence; only post‑lock archived artifacts reported here serve as evidence. Key interpretive caveat required by the run: the preregistered generation_semantics was shared_initial_candidate and the deterministic validator accepted every shared candidate (validator_reject_count=0; repair_calls=0). Therefore the Guarded intervention was empirically inert on this task bank and adapter; this manuscript frames the run as a reproducible boundary case rather than evidence for or against validator utility in general. All archived files and SHA‑256 hashes are released to enable exact reproduction and follow‑on preregistered experiments.
limitations: Single model and adapter (gpt‑5‑mini via hosted_netops_gvr_v1); results do not generalize to other LLMs, adapters, or model families.

Preregistered generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate: because the validator accepted every identical shared candidate (validator_reject_count=0), the Guarded condition was not exercised and the confirmatory hypotheses about validator efficacy could not be tested on these data.
Public/synthetic intent bank and emulated execution limit realism vs production traces and hardware; scorer behavior depends on emulator fidelity.
No injected positive controls in the preserved run; archived artifacts alone cannot demonstrate scorer/validator sensitivity to adversarial or pathological inputs without new execution.
External validity limited: vendor/device diversity, adversarial prompts, and long‑term deployment dynamics are not covered by this run.
